$comment: Known-failing eval rows, as DATA — adding or removing one is a config edit, never a code change.
WHAT THIS IS NOT: this file does NOT affect `eval/run.mjs`, its verdicts, or its exit code.
`pnpm eval` stays red while a real defect is open, because it is also a release gate and a gate
that goes green over an open defect is worse than no gate. This file is read ONLY by
`scripts/eval-gate.mjs` (`pnpm gate`), and only to decide whether a failing row should BLOCK a
task from being called done. Acknowledgement is a property of the gate's report, not of grading.
WHAT AN ENTRY MEANS: 'this row is failing, we know why, it is filed, and a human decided it must
not block unrelated work until it changes'. It does NOT mean 'hidden'. Every acknowledged row is
still NAMED on every gate run, with its issue id — closing the report does not close the
obligation to chase the vendor or retire the capability (L-2).
STALE ENTRIES BLOCK, AND THAT IS THE POINT: when an acknowledged row starts passing, or stops
appearing in the matrix at all, the gate fails and names it. Without that, this list would only
ever grow — a blindfold assembled one honest decision at a time. Clearing a stale entry costs
one line of JSON, which is why blocking on it is the cheapest guard here.
KEY: '<chain>/<capability>', exactly as the eval reports them. A chain-less row (the server and
registry checks) uses the em-dash the eval itself prints: '—/<capability>'.
`issue` MUST reference a record that exists in docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md. An acknowledgement without
a filed issue is just silence with extra steps.

base/token.holders.why: Blockscout's holders endpoint does not answer for base within our 5s hop ceiling. Re-measured 2026-08-11 at a 15s ceiling: still no answer, while /api/v2/stats on the same host with the same key returns in 0.77s. Vendor-side latency on this ENDPOINT; the ceiling is doing its job and raising it is forbidden by the issue's own Do-not. There is also no second route to switch to: measured the same day, the keyless public instance base.blockscout.com times out on the same request, and a warm instance makes the facade fast on arbitrum seconds later — one backend index behind both.

polygon/token.holders.why: Same endpoint, same measurement. Named here rather than hidden: this row became acknowledgeable only when RF-9 stopped reporting a transport timeout as `rate-limited`, which had kept an open vendor failure out of the failure set entirely. (When written, this entry noted arbitrum as 'in the same class but not in the eval chain set'; arbitrum now appears in the matrix and has its own entry.)

arbitrum/token.holders.why: Same endpoint, same 5s hop-ceiling timeout as base and polygon. This row is the DIFFERENT-DAY re-measurement L-12's fix-path item 1 asked for, and it answers that question badly: on 2026-08-11 arbitrum answered the facade in 2.05s once the shared backend was warm, and on 2026-08-12 it timed out on two independent gate runs. The set is widening rather than recovering. Acknowledged so it does not block unrelated work, NOT because it is settled — L-12 now carries the owner decision between routing token.holders to the paid source (L-6 fix-path item 1, a budget call) and retiring the capability.

arbitrum/pairs.active.why: The keyless SEARCH endpoint is a global relevance ranking queried by NATIVE SYMBOL, and the adapter then filters its rows by chainId — so a chain whose ticker does not rank on itself is filtered to nothing. Measured 2026-08-20, 30 rows per response: q=BNB returned 0 of 30 on bsc (all 30 on solana), q=POL 0 of 30 on polygon, q=AVAX 0 of 30 on avalanche. The defect is OLDER than the change that revealed it: until task 014-32a the matrix declared this capability on three chains, all of which happen to rank on themselves, and every other chain was refused before the query ran — L-18's own title names that shape (the gate counted each refusal as a pass). Acknowledged rather than fixed here because the query strategy belongs to task 014-32c, which already owns this adapter's route work; narrowing coverage again to hide it would re-file L-18.
